attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-28
attempts.entry_title: Prefrontal excitation and inhibition during hippocampal sharp-wave ripples (Jadhav et al. 2016)
attempts.summary: The W-track rats learned the task, and the paper's coordinated CA1-PFC reactivation held in direction: CA1-PFC pairs were correlated across sharp-wave ripples above shuffled levels, theta cofiring predicted that correlation, CA1 led PFC, and these relations were absent in rest before the task. The central count did not reproduce: 19 of 167 PFC cells were ripple-modulated, against 56 of 165 in the paper, and no reading tried closed the gap, as the paper leaves its ripple detection details open. With so few modulated cells, most comparisons between excited and inhibited PFC groups, in theta locking, firing properties and spatial correlation, failed. The Y-track results could not be tested, as those rats are not in the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Jadhav, Rothschild, Roumis and Frank (2016) on CRCNS hc-28, which holds simultaneous CA1 and prefrontal recordings from the three rats that learned the W-track alternation task. It detects SWRs from the LFP, classifies PFC cells as SWR-excited, SWR-inhibited or unmodulated, and compares theta locking, spatial and behavioral firing, CA1-PFC SWR correlations, GLM predictions and the pre-task rest. The three Y-track rats of the paper are not in the data set.

findings.statement: The data descriptor gives cellinfo spikewidth as peak to trough width in ms, but the values (0.98 to 23.12, median 9.89) are 30 kHz samples, identical to the spikes files' spikewidth, which the descriptor gives in points. Read as ms, every cell would be excluded from the paper's fast-spiking rule.

The data descriptor says pos data is Nx7; the run-epoch position files have 9 columns (time x y dir vel x-sm y-sm dir-sm vel-sm) and the rest-epoch files 5 (time x y dir vel). In run epochs the unsmoothed columns start with NaN. The pixel size is stored as cmperpixel (0.50 to 0.70), where the descriptor says cmperpix, and the descriptor does not say that x and y are already in cm; the track geometry (centre arm 58 to 81) shows they are.

On days 6 to 8 the second run of each rat is in an environment named wtr2, which the descriptor does not define; it says the rats ran the W-track for 8 days and then novel and familiar environments for the final 3 days, while the files hold 8 days with wtr2 runs in the last 3. The wtr2 track is a different W-track: it sits elsewhere in the camera frame, and for HPa and HPb its centre arm points another way. Which epochs are novel, and whether the 2016 paper used them, is not stated.
Units are indexed by day, tetrode and cluster number only; no identifier links a unit across days, so the paper's unique-unit counts (Table S1) cannot be checked.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the paper's authors on SWR detection: was an SWR an event on any one ripple tetrode, on the mean of tetrodes, or on several tetrodes at once; did the intermediate-CA1 tetrodes that tetinfo marks riptet take part; where was the onset set (threshold crossing or the earlier return to the mean); and what envelope smoothing and minimum duration were used? Here an event on any one ripple tetrode with the onset at the return to the mean gives 415 SWRs per W-track day but only 19 of 167 SWR-modulated PFC cell-days, against 56 of 165 in the paper. The mean-envelope reading matches the paper's duration and low-speed rate but finds 139 SWRs per day, and gives 17 excited and 3 inhibited of 136 PFC cell-days.

Question for the paper's authors on SWR modulation: what span did the SWR-aligned rasters and the circular jitter cover, and what PSTH bin or smoothing entered the squared-difference measure? With a -500 to +500 ms raster, 10 ms bins and jitter over the whole raster, 12 PFC cell-days are excited and 7 inhibited, against 30 and 26 in Table S2; 50 ms bins and a -1 to +1 s raster do not close the gap.

Question for the paper's authors: did the W-track analyses include the second run of days 6 to 8 (environment wtr2 in the task files)? This attempt includes it, following the SEP's statement that data were pooled across all sessions within a day.

entries.title: Prefrontal excitation and inhibition during hippocampal sharp-wave ripples (Jadhav et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Jadhav, Rothschild, Roumis and Frank (2016) on CRCNS hc-28, which holds simultaneous CA1 and prefrontal recordings from the three rats that learned the W-track alternation task. It detects SWRs from the LFP, classifies PFC cells as SWR-excited, SWR-inhibited or unmodulated, and compares theta locking, spatial and behavioral firing, CA1-PFC SWR correlations, GLM predictions and the pre-task rest. The three Y-track rats of the paper are not in the data set.
